text:
miriam: CI started failing on our TS SDK tests after we switched the package to ESM. error: "Cannot use import statement outside a module" and a bunch of module resolution stack traces. tests run fine locally with node 20.
jonah: can you paste the exact error? is this vitest or jest in CI? different fixes.
miriam: vitest in our monorepo, but we also have a few Jest legacy test files. main failure trace (vitest) shows failure when importing '@redwood/inference' from a helper mock: 
```
Error: Must use import to load ES Module: /repo/packages/sdk/dist/index.js
require() of ES Module not supported.
```
shilpa: Sounds like the SDK's build is ESM-only. Vitest (esbuild) sometimes pre-bundles deps with CJS assumptions. Try telling Vitest to inline the package so it gets transformed by your TS pipeline.
jonah: yup — in vitest config: 
```
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    deps: {
      inline: ['@redwood/inference']
    },
    environment: 'node'
  }
})
```
jonah: inline forces vite to not pre-bundle and lets esbuild/ts compile ESM sources. also set environment to node if you need node globals; if you're targeting edge runtime in tests, environment: 'jsdom' or 'happy-dom' might be better.
miriam: we tried inline and it helped a bit, but then mocks broke: vi.mock('@redwood/inference', () => ({ createClient: vi.fn() })) — now it still imports the real file.
pete: order-of-operations: if the package executes side effects at import time (top-level code), inlining will execute real module before your vi.mock gets applied. for vitest you can use 
```
vi.stubGlobal('globalThis', globalThis)
vi.mock('@redwood/inference', async () => {
  return await import('./__mocks__/inference.mjs')
})
```
pete: or move to a manual mock file and use `vi.unmock()` / `vi.mock()` at the top of the test file before any imports.
shilpa: alternative: provide a CJS-compatible test entry point for the SDK build (dist/cjs) alongside ESM (dist/esm). then add exports map so test runner can require a CJS entry.
miriam: we don't want to change the SDK build right now. any Jest-specific tips? we have a couple of Jest tests still.
jonah: for Jest + ESM, use ts-jest with ESM preset or babel-jest. example: 
```
// jest.config.cjs
module.exports = {
  preset: 'ts-jest/presets/default-esm',
  transform: {
    '^.+\\.ts$': 'ts-jest'
  },
  extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts']
}
```
jonah: also set `globals: { 'ts-jest': { useESM: true } }` if using ts-jest.
miriam: ok noted. another issue: edge runtime tests rely on globalThis.fetch and ReadableStream; CI node image is 18 and missing web streams. any suggestions to polyfill for vitest only?
shilpa: you can add a setup file in vitest config: 
```
// vitest.config.ts
test: {
  setupFiles: './test/setup-edge-polyfills.ts'
}
```
shilpa: and in setup-edge-polyfills.ts: 
```
import 'node-fetch/polyfill'
// or
import { ReadableStream } from 'web-streams-polyfill/ponyfill'
globalThis.ReadableStream = ReadableStream
```
pete: for fetch mocking in tests I like 'msw' (node) or just vi.fn on globalThis.fetch. but ensure you polyfill before any module imports that use fetch.
miriam: tests still flaky in CI: sometimes they pass, then fail with ESM:// ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED when resolving deep import to dist/internal. any idea?
jonah: check your package.json "exports" field. If SDK exports only the top-level ESM entry, deep requires will be blocked. Test helpers that import internals need either an export or use file path to src (not ideal). For vitest in a monorepo you can alias the package to the source dir so imports resolve to source TS directly. Example vite alias: 
```
resolve: { alias: { '@redwood/inference': '/repo/packages/sdk/src' } }
```
jonah: then vitest will compile TS source rather than the published dist with exports restrictions.
miriam: good tip. but our CI runs tests inside package workspace roots sometimes — not the root. aliasing from monorepo root is tricky.
pete: you can use relative alias in each package's vitest config or set workspace-level VITE_RESOLVE alias env var used by all configs.
devx-bot: Reminder: there is an open issue #412 in devex about adding an SDK test-friendly build target. link: https://redwood.company/issue/412
miriam: thanks. final question: typings — we saw TS errors in tests when mocking default export vs named: TS says the module has no default export, but runtime import works. how to keep tests happy?
shilpa: prefer `import * as SDK from '@redwood/inference'` in tests if the package uses named exports. if it's ESM-default-export but compiled to CJS for some consumers, types can be mismatched. Check package.json "types" or index.d.ts. You can use `// @ts-ignore` in test mock files as a short-term band-aid, but better to fix the declaration file.
miriam: wrap-up: steps we're taking — add vitest deps.inline, add setup polyfills, try aliasing to src in CI for flaky tests, and add a temporary manual mock file that we import in tests before other imports. I'll follow up with a PR with config changes.
jonah: if you want I can push a draft vitest config and a minimal setup file to your branch.
miriam: please do — would save time. thanks all :thumbsup:
jonah: I'll open PR later today.
shilpa: fyi I documented the ts-jest preset snippet in the devex wiki.
miriam: resolved for now, marking as actionable. I filed a tracking todo so we can later add a CJS test target for SDK.
